section: The Blacksmith's Commission and the Kingdom's Past
description: Totorar the Blacksmith and Elaria receive a commission from a mysterious Dark Elf. During the forging, they sense the lingering soul of the Longleaf Kingdom's last guardian, and the secrets behind the Dark Elf begin to surface.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The Aserta Kingdom has been in turmoil lately. The previous king indulged in extravagance and debauchery in his later years and was killed in a duel by his son. This new king, Jack, known for his ruthlessness, did not reduce taxes as his first act upon taking the throne. Instead, he embarked on massive construction projects, building his palace on the nearby White Mountain.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: # As the human bellows, human lightbulb, and human spotlight of the blacksmith shop, Elaria pokes her head out from the back and stops the wind in her hands.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Bored in front of the unlit furnace, hearing movement and someone coming, immediately lifts the door curtain to see who's here to patronize the business.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "10 gold coins... hmm... better ask about custom weapons."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: # Puts on gloves and picks up the Magic Cold Iron to inspect it, while looking at Totorar, eyes asking whether to charge normally or add a premium.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Shakes head, silent. After all, the country is in turmoil. With such good materials, if the price is too high and the customer leaves, that wouldn't be good.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Alright, we might have some wastage. We'll tell you how much in the end."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Looking at these two materials, tries to use the natural senses within to confirm their quality.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Good, then I'll trouble you. I've long heard your shop can deliver in three hours. Let me witness your craftsmanship?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Alright then, I'll, uh... give it a try?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Mm, I believe in you."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It'll take me a while to prepare. Wait a moment, I haven't even lit the furnace."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: # Elaria goes to light the fire first, preparing the furnace for Totorar.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Haha, roughly killed an armor monster, found the wood in a treasure chest, and then the royal family confiscated most of the gold coins."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I'd like to ask, the dagger you want, is it for slashing or for thrusting?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: # To ensure the sale of the blacksmith shop's weapons, had long ago polished all the unsold weapons in the shop to make them appear sharper and tougher, but they still didn't sell... (Can use spiritual power, right? If so, can polish them.)

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Toto's mouth fires questions at the other like a machine gun.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I dunno, just use your best skills."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Even so, I still want to ask, do you want inscriptions on this weapon, enchantments? Of course, the effects will be better, but relatively, the money will also..."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Whatever artisan soul, life inscriptions, bring it all out. I'm not short on money."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: After confirming, goes to the back room, looks at these two large ingots, and falls into deep thought.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Time to start forging...!

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: When the fire is at its purest, holds this blue-tinged iron ingot in both hands, ready to put both hands and the ingot into the furnace.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: —— Materials added: Magic Cold Iron, Dragon's Saliva Wood.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: # Pays attention to the flame temperature, controlling the bellows intensity with spiritual power.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: The wood in the furnace fire is quite unusual. Found it while traveling specifically to a lush, fantastical forest where vegetation ran rampant, even the elves living there were troubled by it, so brought back a lot of wood from there.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: The flames do not burn the hands. Instead, the palms concentrate the flames in one spot, impacting the cold iron like a blowtorch.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: [Forest Artisan Totorar] awakens her own power:

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: .sh insight d4

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: —— You notice that the water under the warrior's boat shows no trace of blood, yet the gradually sinking corpses and weapons remain clearly visible. You vaguely recall a legend from the distant south, about a white lake. Nothing can float on that lake, except the resolve of those fighting with their backs to the water. The armored man before you has clearly just endured a fierce battle, ending with him gravely wounded and near death, while all his enemies lie slain. Now, breathing shallowly, he finally lifts his gaze. His eyes hold a wintry, solemn lethality. "So I am already dead." He says calmly, the killing intent fading from his eyes.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Toto senses the man's emotions, his heart filled with determination —__—

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Yes, you are dead. But your longsword inherited your resolve to face a thousand armies and ultimately returned to being an iron ingot."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I see." The man tries to rise but aggravates his wounds, forcing him to remain as he was. "May I ask you a question?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Please, we will do our best."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Has the Longleaf Kingdom fallen?" The Longleaf Kingdom, in the records of the Aserta Kingdom, is a dynasty mentioned in but a single line: "Winter, marched against the Longleaf Kingdom, victory." The man seems to have guessed something, yet he waits steadfastly for an answer, even if it will weary him, burden him, or make him abandon the will to live. He must ask. Because he is already dead. So he can question the living.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Nods silently. "But..." "In truth, the Aserta Kingdom itself is now in peril."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Yes, the Longleaf Kingdom is but a single line in the records. Resisting a thousand armies but failing to break the enemy's vanguard—such resolve could only delay the outcome." "If you are tired, rest. Even if a kingdom falls, as long as its people hold Longleaf in their hearts, it is not truly gone. It merely lacks an opportunity. There will always be those willing, daring to face it."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "……… People can slay a thousand living beings, yet they cannot stop a kingdom's fall. Even if it is their homeland, the sole refuge of their souls."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The man falls silent for a long while... ...After a long time, he lets out a deep sigh: "Pitiful." ————— The Magic Cold Iron has been refined. Obtained Emotional Fragment: What is Pitiful? You snap back to reality, returning before the forging table where the formed dagger blade lies. According to the process, it must now be fully shaped before being fitted with the Dragon's Saliva Wood. Then, the artisan's spirit must be imbued, followed by carving the Fate Pattern.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "The Fate Pattern... should we ask, or do it ourselves?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Wait."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The Dark Elf blinks. "Huh, it really can be this fast? So far, all the information that person provided has been correct... No, better think it over again." She seems to be talking to herself...?

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "While it's not yet set, we have some time."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Shifting focus back, the now red-hot cold iron is retrieved. After forging and a slight quench, the blade glimmers with a blue-green sheen under the furnace light.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: # It seems I don't need to pump the bellows myself, so I'll look for some ordinary, hard crystals later. Based on my observations of the Dark Elf, I'll carve them to roughly the right prescription (I'll make a pair of glasses).

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Toto frowns slightly. How to attach this hilt? Looking at the Dragon's Saliva Wood, then at the blade blank.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Pick it up and try. Maybe it's like forging the cold iron ingot."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: —— The Magic Cold Iron is fully formed. —— Thus, only three items remain from the Longleaf Kingdom. So, you go to make the glasses ()

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Envisions countless dagger hilt designs suitable for both forward and reverse grips.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Call me if you need more help, I can stop anytime." # After telling Totorar, I look at the Dark Elf. "What kind of grip do you prefer, and any requirements for the appearance?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I'm thinking about which part of the Dragon's Saliva Tree this wood is from."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hmm... reverse grip. No requirements for appearance, just comfortable to hold. Oh, and preferably good for stabbing, from below upwards."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Trunk, roots, branches—different parts require different carving force."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Emmm"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Envisions a nimble elf crouching down, stabbing upwards at an enemy with a reverse-grip, swinging arm motion. "In that case..." Toto takes out his marvelous tool: the Bacchus Chisel. Called a chisel, it's actually an engraver for inscriptions and can also shape the Dragon's Saliva Wood. Securing the rough Dragon's Saliva Wood on the table, he focuses on shaving off burrs and carving.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: # Add a glow to Totorar's chisel and soften it a bit to avoid shadows interfering with the final product.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Toto narrows his eyes.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: ———— Standing before the forging table, your minds drift once more, entering the spirit within the Dragon's Saliva Wood. This is a lush, verdant forest. Looking back, you see a massive cave-bottom nest, pitch-black and showing no signs of life. Just as you wonder, a dark shadow flashes by and stops before you. Looking closely, this seems to be... a dragon...?! Fortunately, it's just a juvenile dragon, not yet very aggressive. "Who are you?" The black juvenile dragon speaks. "What are you doing near my home?"
